article_limitations: Disposition aggregate_only: the source reports five pediatric Dubberley type 2A capitellum fractures only as a series (mean or range values and all-patient statements); no patient has individual identity evidence, so no individual patient records are created and series statements are not copied to placeholder patients.
reported_individual_count is 5 (literal) and roster_complete is false because none of the five stated individuals can be enumerated.
Source conflict on the surgical approach: the abstract says a posterolateral approach, while the case presentation and discussion say a lateral approach through the Kaplan interval.

Source conflict on follow-up: a minimum of 12 months in all five cases (case presentation), a mean follow-up of 8.8 months (abstract) and a last follow-up six months postoperatively (Figure 4 caption).

The abstract reports transient stiffness in two patients that resolved with physiotherapy, while the results report a 12-degree extension deficit and a 15-degree flexion deficit in two unnamed patients at the last follow-up and the discussion calls them minor limitations; these are not reconciled.
Figures 1 to 4 show one or more unidentified series members; ownership is unresolved and they are not EHR-includable. Pixels were reviewed in the separate visual target.
